m2c/src/m2c/interact/__init__.py -- Patch L01a: the two tools that talk to the person, ``ask_user`` and ``tasks``.

What this package is
--------------------
The pure, screen-free half of two device-executed tools (protocol/v1 ``tools/ask_user.json`` and ``tools/tasks.json``).
Nothing here draws anything, reads a setting, touches a file or opens a link:

    question.py  ``ask_user``: ``parse_question`` (the model's arguments -> a ``UserQuestion``, or a fixed error),
                 the answer types and ``answer_text`` (what the model reads back).  Also the ``QuestionCallable``
                 interface a screen implements (L01b does, for the terminal UI).
    tasks.py     ``tasks``: ``parse_tasks`` (the model's whole list -> a tuple of ``Task``, or a fixed error), the
                 one-line confirmation and the ``TaskSink`` interface a screen implements.

The runner (m2c/runner.py) does the waiting, the timing and the wiring; this package only decides what is valid
and what text goes back to the model.

Rules both modules keep
-----------------------
* Fail closed with a FIXED message.  An error names the rule that failed ("option labels must be unique") and never
  repeats anything the model wrote: a label, an id or a title could carry anything, and an error is logged and
  returned to the model.
* Text that reaches a terminal later (a question, a label, a title) holds no control characters: an escape
  sequence in a label could move the cursor or fake a prompt.  Newli

m2c/src/m2c/interact/question.py -- Patch L01a: ``ask_user``, the request, the answer and their rules.

The model asks one question and waits.  It may offer up to six options (each a short label and an optional line of
explanation) and may allow the person to answer in their own words.  The call ends in one of four ways, and the
runner turns each into a ``tool_result``:

    answered   ``ok`` true; the text built here by ``answer_text`` ("The person answered." and then one
               ``Chose: <label>`` line per option and a ``Wrote: <words>`` line);
    declined   ``ok`` false, fixed text (the person closed the question without answering);
    timed out  ``ok`` false, fixed text (``timeout_s`` passed with no answer);
    no person  ``ok`` false, fixed text (headless run, or a screen that cannot ask).

The functions here are pure.  ``parse_question`` is the second line of defence behind the policy engine's type check
(C06 only knows an argument's JSON type, not "at most six options" or "labels are unique") and the first line of
defence for the rules a JSON schema cannot say.  It raises ``QuestionError`` with a FIXED message that names the rule
and never repeats what the model wrote.  ``answer_text`` is the check on the OTHER side: the screen is code too, and
a buggy or hostile one must not be able to put an option the model never offered, or a type that is not text, into
the model's context.

m2c/src/m2c/interact/tasks.py -- Patch L01a: the ``tasks`` list, its validation and the interface a screen implements.

The model keeps a task list for the work in hand and sends the WHOLE list on every call; the new list replaces the old
one and an empty list clears it.  ``parse_tasks`` turns the arguments into a tuple of frozen ``Task`` values or fails
closed with a FIXED message that names the rule and never repeats an id or a title (they are the model's text).

What a JSON schema cannot say is checked here: ids are unique, every ``depends_on`` names a task in the same list and
the dependencies do not form a cycle.  The rules run in a fixed order and the first one that fails is reported:

    list shape -> too many -> each task (shape, id, title, status, depends_on) -> duplicate ids ->
    unknown dependency -> cycle

The list is shown to the person by a ``TaskSink`` (the screen; L01b implements one for the terminal UI) and recorded in
the local event store (type ``tasks``, see the runner).  A task's title is text the model wrote and goes to a terminal,
so it holds no control characters and is a single line.

Standard library only.

Place this file at: m2c/src/m2c/interact/tasks.py
